sentences.text: IBAC and the Victorian Ombudsman jointly investigated allegations that publicly funded staff and resources were used for ALP factional activity, including branch stacking.
sentences.support:
Operation Watts, a coordinated investigation into allegations of misuse of ministerial and Members’ staff and other 
budget entitlements for internal ALP purposes, including branch stacking

sentences.text: The investigation focused on the Moderate Labor faction and examined staff deployment, employment practices and grants to associated community organisations.
sentences.support:
The misconduct centred 
on the appointment and misuse of electorate 
officers and ministerial staff to pursue ML 
factional agendas

sentences.text: The two bodies found that staff were extensively diverted to factional work during paid hours and that two MPs breached conduct codes.
sentences.support:
We concluded that two MPs breached one or more 
elements of the Ministerial Code of Conduct and the 
MPs’ Code of Conduct.

sentences.text: The bodies could not quantify the misuse and said difficulties of proof prevented them from recommending prosecution.
sentences.support:
the difficulties in proof are such that we 
cannot recommend prosecution.

sentences.text: The bodies made 21 reform recommendations, including an ethics committee, an independent parliamentary integrity commissioner, tighter staff-employment rules and stronger grant oversight.
sentences.support:
the government and the parliament work together to establish a Parliamentary Integrity 
Commissioner as an independent officer of the parliament

findings.quote:
There was extensive misuse of staff for factional 
or party-specific purposes during business 
hours.

We concluded that two MPs breached one or more 
elements of the Ministerial Code of Conduct and the 
MPs’ Code of Conduct.

Factional members or their relatives were given 
publicly funded employment in electorate or 
ministerial offices as a reward for recruiting 
members or working for the faction.

It has not been possible to determine the 
extent of factional work done during office 
hours during the period under investigation, 
but it undoubtedly involved a very substantial 
misuse of public resources.

Despite the allegations that were, in part, the 
reason for establishing Operation Watts, no 
evidence was uncovered that such grants were 
used to pay for ALP memberships.

notes: This is a joint IBAC and Victorian Ombudsman report. The Foreword supplies the report-level summary; its prose ends on PDF page 8, with only a running header extracted on PDF page 9. Recommendations 1 to 21 were read in Chapter 8. The inability to quantify misuse and difficulties supporting prosecution are retained. The summary uses no personal names.
